overall_limitations: Gold matches are assessed per claim. Several composite rubric facts are distributed across claims without being fully stated by any single claim, including synchronization order, FULL reader behavior, bidirectional hook replacement, and busy fallback.

The claims omit reader end-mark fixation, WAL-index lookup and same-host constraints, one-writer serialization, explicit connection-local autocheckpoint configuration, commit-latency consequences, read amplification, and multi-database error propagation.
S1 and S2 differ on reader blocking and unconditional completion language. f25 accurately attributes its narrower statement to S2, but the packet does not reconcile the descriptions.
The threshold trigger in f18 must be read with f19's non-positive-N disabling exception.
The historical claims concern WAL page-writing behavior; they do not establish checkpoint origins or checkpoint-mode introduction dates.
The pass statistics do not establish semantic depth or research saturation.
